Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’m starting with the workspace contract and the current rollout evidence. I’ll use the required `fish-control-primitives` skill for the structured transfer, and the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill to inspect both moving-window views before touching the policy.

The inherited bank shows this is a later iteration: four repeated line-of-sight-response captures established fixed-condition determinism, but all share isolated posterior angle contact and substantial speed/acceleration saturation. I’m now checking the actual sampled traces and both visual rows to distinguish the two apparent success variants before choosing the one mechanism this candidate will test.

The visual comparison confirms the guard did what the traces say: it kept the same body-attached alternating wake and late target-line turn while removing contact and lowering force/moment peaks. The remaining defect has shifted upstream to velocity headroom—about 18% of anterior samples and 4.5% of posterior samples still sit at the speed cap—so I’m testing whether a compact predictive speed-envelope filter can act only on commands that are still accelerating an already-fast joint.

The candidate now keeps every evidenced navigation and propulsion branch intact and adds only a symmetric speed-feasibility projection after the successful angle guard. I also revised the reusable lesson to convert the former “test a stopping-margin guard” hypothesis into a completed positive result, with the remaining velocity-saturation boundary stated separately. Next I’m auditing activation, reflection symmetry, schema coverage, and the required checker contract—without running CFD.

The mandated checker agent was invoked, but its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable on this account. I’m following the checker’s own fallback precedent: running its three prescribed non-CFD commands separately, then I’ll repair and rerun any failure.

All three mandated checks now pass. The final static audit also confirms 41/41 parameter references are declared, the new projection is reflection-equivariant, and its frozen-trace effect is targeted: it removes every outward request at observed speed-cap states while leaving opposing acceleration untouched. I’m doing one last scope and content review now.

Produced exactly one candidate: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl). It adds a symmetric normalized joint-speed feasibility projection while preserving the successful line-of-sight controller and angle guard.

Updated:

- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md)

All required non-CFD checks pass: material guidance update, finite two-joint contract, 41-field parameter schema, and editable-boundary check. Reflection and frozen-trace audits also pass. The checker agent was invoked but its pinned model was unavailable, so its prescribed commands were run directly. No CFD was run.
